review_comments.body: **Fallback masks storage failures** When a new-layout read encounters a transient S3 failure, permission error, or another non-missing I/O error, this catch treats it as a missing key and retries the legacy location. That can return stale legacy content or discard the original storage failure.

**URI views lose metadata** `URI_VIEW` now returns before MIME type and length are assigned. The previous implementation fetched metadata and populated these fields for every supported view, so callers using URI references now receive `ComplexData` with missing metadata.
Artifacts
**[Focused URI\_VIEW metadata comparison test source](https://app.greptile.com/trex/artifacts/68adbf27-c21c-4be2-b25e-769173842d26)** - The authored JUnit test saves text complex data and asserts URI\_VIEW exposes its MIME type and stored length, with the takeaway that both revisions were exercised using the same assertion. **[Parent URI\_VIEW metadata execution output](https://app.greptile.com/trex/artifacts/6049f004-3156-48c8-90bf-8a09d8d8671e)** - The focused Maven test executed against the parent revision and passed with one test and zero failures, with the takeaway that URI\_VIEW previously populated the asserted metadata. **[PR URI\_VIEW metadata execution output](https://app.greptile.com/trex/artifacts/ba03b9a9-0a90-4a57-a108-26945b1de43e)** - The identical focused Maven test executed against PR head and failed because expected text/plain was null, with the takeaway that the PR loses URI\_VIEW MIME metadata.
Ran code and verified through T-Rex

**Storage implementations lose compatibility** Adding `getDataWithMetadata` as an abstract interface method breaks independently compiled module `StorageService` implementations that predate this API. Once a complex-observation handler invokes the method, the JVM throws `AbstractMethodError`. Provide a default compatibility implementation, such as combining the existing data and metadata methods, or introduce an opt-in extension interface.
Artifacts
**[Authored ABI harness source](https://app.greptile.com/trex/artifacts/d283bb2e-3422-445a-8699-062d5171888f)** - This isolated Java 21 harness compiles a legacy implementation against the old interface and invokes the modeled complex-observation handler against compatibility and abstract interface variants, with the takeaway that it directly tests the requested ABI boundary. **[Before execution log (default compatibility method)](https://app.greptile.com/trex/artifacts/7d91b3f7-91fc-4452-beb2-a639ae6a87bb)** - The Java 21 compatibility run dispatches the same invokeinterface call to an inherited default method and returns legacy-data:obs-key|metadata with exit code 0, with the takeaway that a default method preserves this legacy implementation. **[After execution log (new abstract method)](https://app.greptile.com/trex/artifacts/f88318af-0a60-489e-af61-0aa6b0e85ee0)** - The Java 21 PR-shaped abstract-method run throws AbstractMethodError at ComplexObservationHandler.read after invoking getDataWithMetadata on the independently compiled legacy implementation and exits 1, with the takeaway that the proposed abstract API addition breaks that runtime path. **[Relevant PR source lines](https://app.greptile.com/trex/artifacts/113b39e2-d82e-44cb-b1b1-5aad94737e8d)** - This captured PR diff shows the abstract StorageService declaration and the AbstractHandler getObs call sites that dispatch to it, with the takeaway that the executed ABI reproduction matches the changed production call path.

review_comments.body:
At the StorageService level this really is one probe, but `LocalStorageService.getPath()` runs its own `Files.exists(legacyPath)` on every call, and it gets reached three times per read on this path: once inside `exists()`, once more when `exists()` stats the resolved path, and once inside `getDataWithMetadata()`.

I instrumented `LocalStorageService` and ran `AbstractHandler.getObs`, `TextHandler.getObs(TEXT_VIEW)` and `BinaryDataHandler.getObs(RAW_VIEW)` on this branch and on master. All three give the same counts:

```
master:      4 x Files.exists + 1 x newInputStream + 1 x readAttributes = 6
this branch: 3 x Files.exists + 1 x readAttributes + 1 x newInputStream = 5
```

The duplicate metadata fetch is genuinely gone, which is the part this set out to do. But TRUNK-6682 asks for "at most one existence-related check", and it counts `getPath()`'s probe explicitly when it tallies the per-read cost, so on local storage a read lands at five filesystem calls rather than at the "single combined data+metadata read on the happy path" the PR description claims.

The probes that are left are the ones ibacher's feedback deliberately kept, so I am not asking you to revisit that. What I would like settled before this merges is the ticket: does TRUNK-6682 stay open for the layout-resolution half, with this PR closing only the duplicate-metadata part?

This early return loses the legacy filename fallback a few lines further down, the `extensions.contains(filename)` block carrying the TRUNK-6472 comment. Master reached it on this path because it logged the failure and carried on into the shared tail.

With `valueComplex = "jpg|2026/01-01/2026-01-01-00-00-00-000-abcdefgh.jpg"` and the file absent, master hands back a `ComplexData` titled `/2026/01-01/2026-01-01-00-00-00-000-abcdefgh.jpg`, and this branch hands back one titled `jpg`. The data is null either way, so nothing throws and no test notices; the obs just loses the only name identifying it.

Keeping master's single exit fixes it: initialise `dwm` to null, let the catch log without returning, and skip the read block when `dwm` is null. The `dwm.metadata()` call further down is already behind `img != null`, which cannot be reached when `dwm` is null.

2.8.0 was tagged a long time ago (2.8.9 is out) and master is 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT, so a module author who trusts this tag and sets `require_version 2.8.0` gets a `NoClassDefFoundError` the first time a handler hands them one of these. It wants the version this actually lands in, plus whatever maintenance lines it gets backported to. `StorageService.getDataWithMetadata` and the new `injectMissingMetadata` overload have no `@since` at all.
